reason: "Every observable" holds only at T=0; at finite T observables are universal functions of T/T_F. Neutron matter is universal only approximately.

fix.summary: At a Feshbach resonance the scattering length diverges and drops out. With negligible range, density (k_F) and T are the only scales, so thermodynamics is universal: at T=0 a number times the free-Fermi-gas value (Bertsch ξ), otherwise a function of T/T_F. Dilute neutron matter is approximately unitary.

reason: The hole argument did not start the substantivalism–relationism debate (Newton–Leibniz). It revived that debate via Stachel (1980) and Earman–Norton (1987).

fix.summary: Einstein's 1913 hole argument made generally covariant field equations look indeterministic: diffeomorphism-related solutions agree outside a region and differ inside it. His 1915 point-coincidence resolution (points have no identity apart from the metric) let him accept covariance. Stachel and Earman–Norton revived it as the centre of the modern substantivalism debate.

reason: The CPT theorem also needs a Hermitian Hamiltonian and the spectral condition. Greenberg's 'CPT violation implies Lorentz violation' is contested (Chaichian et al.).

fix.summary: The CPT theorem follows from Lorentz invariance, locality and a Hermitian Hamiltonian. Greenberg (2002) argued that in interacting local QFT any CPT violation implies Lorentz violation. Kaon mass differences, antihydrogen spectroscopy and Penning-trap particle–antiparticle comparisons therefore constrain the CPT-odd coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.
fix.breaks: Greenberg's implication has been challenged by Chaichian, Dolgov, Novikov and Tureanu (2011). Some CPT tests constrain the SME only within that framework.

reason: 2D CFT applies complex-analysis machinery: a method transfer. Local conformal maps are holomorphic or antiholomorphic; the global group is only SL(2,C).

fix.summary: In two dimensions local conformal maps are holomorphic (or antiholomorphic), so the stress tensor splits into T(z) and T̄(z̄). Radial quantization turns charges into contour integrals, Ward identities and operator-product expansions follow from the residue theorem, and the Virasoro generators are Laurent coefficients.

reason: Analyticity from causality is proved only in limited cases (forward, some fixed-t), and dispersion relations generally need subtractions.

fix.summary: Causality and unitarity imply analyticity of scattering amplitudes in the energy variables (proved for forward and some fixed-t cases, postulated more generally). Amplitudes therefore obey dispersion relations, possibly subtracted: the relativistic Kramers–Kronig. Optical theorem and Cutkosky rules give cut discontinuities; the unitarity method rebuilds loop amplitudes from cuts.

reason: MSW is not in general adiabatic passage; adiabatic conversion is the solar-neutrino regime of the matter effect.

fix.summary: Flavour and mass eigenstates are related by the unitary PMNS matrix, so oscillation is the time evolution of a superposition of energy eigenstates. The two-flavour formula is the two-level Rabi-type formula. In the Sun, the MSW effect acts as adiabatic passage through an avoided crossing of the matter Hamiltonian's eigenvalues.

reason: An identity cannot carry a breaks. 'Gauge field = connection' is exact; the GR comparison belongs in the summary as a qualified parallel.

fix.summary: A gauge potential is a connection on a principal bundle, its field strength is the curvature, Wilson loops are holonomies, and the Bianchi identity DF=0 holds. GR's spin connection and Riemann tensor are the same structures, except that the gravitational connection is soldered to the tangent bundle and fixed by the metric.

fix.summary: LHC searches are hypothesis tests: profile-likelihood ratios with systematics as nuisance parameters, Wilks/Wald asymptotics giving Z = √q₀, CLs for exclusions, and look-elsewhere corrections, as in the 2012 Higgs discovery. 'Only loophole' holds only under the theorem's assumptions (massive particles, d>2, nontrivial S-matrix); conformal symmetry escapes when massless. This is method transfer, not identity.

fix.summary: Coleman–Mandula forbids Lie-group S-matrix symmetries that mix spacetime and internal symmetries non-trivially, given a mass gap, d>2 and nontrivial scattering. Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius showed that graded algebras with fermionic generators (supersymmetry, closing on momentum) are the only extension; massless theories also allow conformal symmetry.

reason: Pure power-law scaling with an anomalous dimension holds only at a fixed point. Away from one, scaling is governed by the running coupling.

fix.summary: Quantum loops break naive dimensional analysis: the renormalization scale μ enters, so at a fixed point correlators scale with engineering plus anomalous dimension (Barenblatt's incomplete similarity). Away from fixed points the running coupling governs scaling. Classically scale-free massless QCD generates Λ_QCD, a few hundred MeV, from a dimensionless coupling.

reason: The Metropolis algorithm (1953) came from equation-of-state statistical mechanics, not neutron transport. The text implies otherwise.

fix.summary: Ulam, von Neumann and Metropolis created the Monte Carlo method in 1946–49 to follow neutron chains in fissile assemblies. MC neutron transport (MCNP, Serpent, OpenMC) still computes reactor k_eff. The approach then spread across physics, including the 1953 Metropolis algorithm for statistical mechanics.
